title: policy-bundle-operator: add install-time & upgrade hooks for private-installer and terraform provider
author: Maya Chen
body:
Context: Private deployments require a deterministic, idempotent way to bootstrap tenant-scoped RBAC and policy bundles during installer runs (both Helm-based private-installer and the Terraform provider path). Motivation: customers upgrading private clusters were observing partial role bindings after failed upgrades and operators had to manually re-run bootstrap scripts. This PR introduces install-time and upgrade hooks in the policy-bundle operator and exposes reconciliation-friendly entrypoints for the Terraform provider and Helm charts so bootstrapping is resilient across install, upgrade, and rollback scenarios.

What this PR does: 1) Adds an 'install-hook' controller mode to the policy-bundle operator that runs a preflight and then applies tenant Role/RoleBinding templated bundles atomically; 2) Introduces a lightweight 'upgrade-hook' flow to validate existing bindings, migrate legacy role names, and perform a canary create+verify before promoting changes cluster-wide; 3) Exposes a stable HTTP readiness endpoint on the operator for the private-installer (Helm) post-install hook and the Terraform provider to poll until RBAC is fully reconciled; 4) Adds idempotent retry semantics and leader-locked bootstrap so multiple installer threads (or retries) do not create duplicate bindings; 5) Adds terraform-provider integration: new resource redwood_policy_bootstrap that invokes the operator's gRPC RPC when running inside VPC/on-prem setups where K8s API access is available; 6) Updates Helm chart hooks (pre-install, pre-upgrade, post-upgrade) to use the operator readiness probe and handle rollbacks by marking resources with the owner reference so Helm can garbage collect on failed installs.

Files touched: high-level operator code (pkg/controller/installhook, pkg/controller/upgradecheck), new grpc/proto bootstrap API, helm charts changes under charts/policy-bundle/templates/hooks.yaml, terraform provider glue under terraform/modules/policy_bootstrap, samples for private-installer.

Testing done: - Unit tests for install-hook and upgrade-check controllers (controller/unit/). - Integration e2e in the perf-canary infra: simulated multi-tenant bootstrap with concurrent Helm retries and Terraform apply loops. - Manual upgrade path testing: migrated a 1.2.0 cluster with legacy role prefixes and validated access matrix via automated smoke suites. - CI: initial run failed due to flakiness in starter leader election; fixed by adding backoff and leader annotation check, reran and green.

Rollback and upgrade notes: the upgrade-hook will attempt a safe migration path by creating new RoleBindings alongside legacy ones, running a verification phase (token-based access checks), then deleting legacy bindings only after verification succeeds. The Helm hooks add a post-upgrade verification step and will fail the release if verification fails; because resources carry owner references, Helm rollback will remove new bindings on failed upgrades. Terraform provider calls are tolerant to transient operator unavailability and will surface a clear diagnostic error (SUP-411) if bootstrap cannot reach the operator endpoint.

Security & compliance: tightened the bootstrap RPC to require mTLS and a bootstrap token signed by the private-installer; added audit log entries for all bootstrap operations (rbac-bootstrap-audit log key).

Release notes: "Policy bundle operator now supports install and upgrade hooks to provide idempotent, observable RBAC bootstrapping for Private deployments (Helm + Terraform). This fixes intermittent missing role bindings after failed upgrades and adds safer migration for legacy role names."

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests added - [x] Helm chart updated - [x] Terraform provider integration implemented - [x] Docs updated (private deployment runbook) - [x] QA smoke and canary passes

Notes for reviewers: focus on the leader election hardening, the semantics of the bootstrap RPC (security posture), and the Helm hook templates — these are the most likely sources of cluster-specific compatibility issues.

b4d1e71: experiments: leader election backoff and annotation probe
c12f5aa: proto: add BootstrapService RPC and bootstrap status enums
d8f7c2e: helm: add pre-install and post-upgrade hooks with readiness polling

reviews: Diego Alvarez (request changes): Leader election looks racy during rapid restarts — can we add a randomized jitter on the retry backoff?
Maya Chen (author): Added jitter and increased maximum backoff in a9c3f2d; also added e2e that simulates restarts.
Priya Nair (comment): Need to ensure Helm hook timeouts are conservative for large air-gapped environments. Consider making timeouts configurable via values.yaml.
Maya Chen (author): Made hook timeout configurable with values.policyBootstrap.hookTimeoutMs and documented rationale in charts/policy-bundle/README.
Samir Gupta (approved): Security review complete; mTLS and bootstrap token approach acceptable. Minor nits in audit log formatting fixed.
CI Bot: initial pipeline failure on scripts/ci/operator_leader_test.sh due to missing nsconfig; rerun resulted in green checks.
release_notes: Policy bundle operator: install-time and upgrade hooks for Private (Helm + Terraform) enabling idempotent RBAC bootstrapping, safer role migrations, and observable verification steps. Includes Terraform resource redwood_policy_bootstrap and Helm hook templates.
notes_for_ops: Operator exposes /ready/bootstrap endpoint. Make sure private-installer and terraform-provider have network path and bootstrap token configured. Audit logs emitted under rbac-bootstrap-audit key.
